title: Negative thermal expansion, lattice dynamics, and complex magnetism in TbFeO$_3$
authors: Shubham Farswan, Reshma Kumawat, Dipankar Sarkar, Deeksha Singh, Md. Atif Hasan, Devajyoti Mukherjee, Kaushik Sen
abstract: We report a temperature-dependent investigation of orthoferrite TbFeO$_3$ using x-ray diffraction, DC magnetization, and Raman scattering, complemented by room-temperature x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. X-ray diffraction reveals negative thermal expansion over 5-300 K, with a small but systematic increase in unit-cell volume upon cooling in the absence of any structural phase transition. Raman scattering measurements identify the Raman-active phonon modes and show clear deviations from the conventional Klemens anharmonic decay model, particularly in phonon frequencies, indicating the presence of spin-phonon coupling. Two modes of $A_g$ and $B_{1g}$ symmetry exhibit a crossover from Gaussian-dominated line shapes at low temperatures to mixed Gaussian-Lorentzian profiles at higher temperatures, reflecting a transition from inhomogeneous broadening to lifetime-driven dynamics. High-energy Raman spectra reveal two-magnon excitations associated with the Fe sublattice, consistent with linear spin-wave theory, whose spectral weight shows only weak temperature dependence. In addition, a broad Raman mode emerging below $\sim 175$ K exhibits an order-parameter-like temperature evolution and coincides with the onset of phonon anomalies, while no corresponding strong anomaly is observed in the two-magnon response. Taken together, these results establish TbFeO$_3$ as a system with pronounced interplay among lattice dynamics, spin correlations, and emergent local magnetic-lattice anomalies.
summary: This work comprehensively investigates the physical properties of TbFeO3 by combining XRD, magnetization, and Raman spectroscopy. Key findings include observing negative thermal expansion and identifying strong evidence of spin-phonon coupling through phonon line shape analysis. The results establish that this material exhibits a pronounced interplay between its lattice structure, magnetic order, and local electronic environment.
main_problem: To investigate the complex interplay among lattice dynamics, spin correlations, and local magnetic anomalies in TbFeO3.
main_result: The study reveals negative thermal expansion without structural transitions, strong evidence of spin-phonon coupling via Raman scattering, and a clear interplay between lattice and magnetic degrees of freedom.
method: A combination of temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction (XRD), DC magnetization measurements, and advanced Raman spectroscopy was employed.
model_or_system: The physical system is the rare-earth orthoferrite TbFeO3, which serves as a model for studying spin-lattice coupling in complex oxides.
key_observables: Negative thermal expansion (NTE) of unit cell volume, phonon frequencies and line shapes, two-magnon excitations, and magnetic susceptibility/magnetization curves.
important_parameters: Temperature range spanning 5 K to 300 K; the crossover from Gaussian to Lorentzian phonon profiles.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that deviations in Raman spectra reflect spin-phonon coupling mechanisms rather than simple anharmonic decay. The interpretation of spectral weight requires careful consideration of background subtraction and fitting models.
figures_summary: Figures show XRD patterns demonstrating anisotropic unit cell volume changes (NTE), temperature dependence of lattice parameters, and Raman spectra detailing phonon modes and two-magnon excitations across various temperatures.
paper_structure: The paper systematically combines structural characterization (XRD for NTE) with spectroscopic probes (Raman for phonons/magnons) and magnetic measurements (magnetization). The structure builds the argument by showing how anomalies in one measurement correlate with subtle changes in another, establishing a unified picture of coupled physics.
why_interesting: The detailed investigation into spin-phonon coupling mechanisms using multiple complementary techniques provides rich data on emergent quantum interactions in insulating magnets, which is relevant for understanding lattice dynamics in correlated materials.

FIG. 2. High-resolution XPS spectra of the Fe-2p and Tb- 3d core levels of TbFeO3, showing the characteristic spin- orbit split components along with deconvoluted contributions corresponding to Fe2+, Fe3+ and Tb3+, Tb4+ ionic states.

FIG. 3. Magnetization as a function of temperature for TbFeO3 measured under an applied magnetic field of 500 Oe: (a) low-temperature regime and (b) high-temperature regime. The inset of panel (a) highlights the variation in magnetization in the vicinity of 280 K. The inset of panel (b) shows the inverse magnetic susceptibility fitted using the modified Curie–Weiss expression given in Eq. (3).

FIG. 4. Temperature-dependent Raman spectra of polycrystalline TbFeO3 measured at 11, 100, 200, and 300 K. Selected phonon modes are assigned, along with two-phonon (2P) and two-magnon (2M) excitations. The arrow indicates the emergence of a new mode at low temperatures.

FIG. 5. Temperature dependence of the integrated intensity of the two-magnon peak in polycrystalline TbFeO3 powder. The inset shows the calculated magnon density of states (MDOS) for the Fe sublattice in TbFeO3, plotted together with the two- magnon Raman spectrum measured at 11 K for comparison.
